study.citation: Choi et al., De novo design of cysteine proteases, bioRxiv 2025.11.21.689808 version 3

question: Can the public version-3 release support one fixed 69-case prospective comparison of sequence and structure baselines against calibrated intended-bond cleavage outcomes?

decision_rule.qualify: The public sources must enumerate all 69 pre-outcome attempts, preserve expression and assay attrition, provide exact paired enzyme and substrate identities, give every negative a comparable quantitative value or calibrated censoring bound, bind every positive product to the intended scissile bond, and expose same-case inputs for both baselines without invented joins.
decision_rule.stop: Any missing cohort rows, qualitative-only negatives, unbound product identity, or unavailable same-case input closes this all-in-one benchmark route. Do not run a model on the top-level 13/69 summary.

cohort.supported: The version-3 abstract reports 13 active designs among 69 tested.
cohort.unresolved: The accessible primary metadata and indexed manuscript text do not enumerate the 69 attempts or expose expression, purification and assay attrition. A positive-led reconstruction would be outcome-selected. The same 13/69 outcome was public in version 1 on 2025-11-22, so a model selected or tuned later cannot be called a prospective test on this cohort.

sequences.supported: Indexed version-3 manuscript text says protein sequences are in Supplementary Table 1 and complete plasmid sequences are in Supplementary Information 1 and 2.
sequences.unresolved: The supplementary bytes and their opaque filenames could not be retrieved or inventoried, so exact 69-row enzyme-to-substrate pairing and translation checks are unavailable.

negative_outcomes.supported: The public manuscript distinguishes active and inactive designs using post-IMAC cleavage state.
negative_outcomes.unresolved: No cohort-wide quantitative measurement, common calibration, detection limit or censoring bound for every inactive design was accessible. A band class cannot support the frozen quantitative comparison.

product_identity.supported: The indexed version-3 manuscript states that LC-MS of SEC-purified samples confirmed all 13 active designs cleaved precisely at the intended target site.
product_identity.unresolved: The inaccessible underlying product table prevents an independent row-level audit and inventory of any secondary products, but the primary prose supports intended-bond identity for the 13 reported positives.

structure_inputs.supported: Six public structures exist: 9YNL, 9YNM, 9YOX, 9YOY, 9YOZ and 9YP0. They cover Dokki_15 C100A complex, Dokki_15 WT apo, Gawi_09 WT apo, HC12 C103A complex, HC12 WT complex and HC34 WT apo.
structure_inputs.unresolved: Six deposited structures are a validation subset, not 69 author design complexes. Exact same-case design inputs for every positive and negative were not exposed by the retrieved sources.

source_access.result: The bioRxiv metadata API confirms version 3, its 2026-09-21 date, abstract and canonical PDF link. Direct version-3 PDF and JATS requests returned HTTP 429. The NCBI OA-package endpoint returned HTTP 404, and the PMC EFetch record explicitly withholds full-text XML. No version-3 supplementary file was retrieved.
source_access.transport_boundary: Search and connector transport bytes are not exposed. Failed HTTP response bodies were not retained.

conclusion.decision: Do not use Choi version 3 as the frozen all-in-one prospective benchmark. Publicly accessible evidence in this audit does not support a lossless 69-row cohort with calibrated negatives and same-case structure inputs; the outcomes have also been public since version 1 in November 2025.
conclusion.scope: This is an evidence-and-access stop for the proposed comparison, not a claim that the study lacks the data, not a criticism of the reported 13/69 result, and not evidence against the designed proteases.
conclusion.external_dependency: A public hashed source bundle containing the complete attempted-design table, cohort-wide quantitative assay values with detection limits and original design complexes would be required to reconstruct the activity screen. A clean prospective specificity benchmark additionally needs a previously unexposed cohort and a matched noncognate cross-target panel.

strongest_alternative.question: Can an already-public exact-sequence protease-substrate panel support a prospective sequence-specificity generalization test even though it does not localize product bonds?
strongest_alternative.why: It preserves a large quantitative set of exact protease-substrate pairs and negatives. It can answer a narrower sequence-specificity question without pretending to validate intended-bond cleavage or de novo enzyme-design success.
strongest_alternative.next_action: Audit its public train/test chronology and raw reporter calibration once, then preregister a family- or substrate-held-out sequence-only baseline if and only if the split can be fixed before scoring.
strongest_alternative.next_stop: Stop if design choices were selected after viewing the same held-out measurements, if exact assayed constructs cannot be reconstructed, or if reporter normalization is not comparable across the proposed split.
